docs.title: OAE PINN Emulator
docs.text:
A physics-informed neural network emulator for 2-D ocean tracer transport used in Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement (OAE) studies.

The project explores machine learning based emulators for tracer evolution using Oceananigans.jl simulations as training while also penalizing advection–diffusion PDE residuals, aiming to stay physically consistent and generalize across forcing.

View code Run demo

docs.title: Tech stack
docs.text:
• Oceananigans.jl simulations → tracer + velocity fields
  • NetCDF outputs → processed with xarray
  • Training in PyTorch (single-step + multi-step variants; physics loss optional)

docs.title: Reproduce
docs.text:
This is a starter reproducibility guide. I’ll make the commands and dataset IDs fully exact once the thesis pipeline is locked.

Goal

You should be able to (1) set up the environment reliably, (2) run a precomputed evaluation (coming soon), and (3) later reproduce training + evaluation from tracked configs.

docs.title: 2) Create the environment (uv)
docs.text:
If the repo contains pyproject.toml + uv.lock:

'''bash uv sync '''

Run any command like:

'''bash uv run python --version '''

Recommended workflow

Prefer uv run ... over manually activating a virtualenv. It keeps runs consistent and reproducible.

docs.title: from the repo root
docs.text:
mkdir -p data outputs '''

  • data/ → NetCDF datasets (Oceananigans output or downloaded sample)
  • outputs/ → checkpoints, predictions, plots, logs

Do not commit large artifacts

Keep NetCDFs, checkpoints, and generated outputs in data//outputs/ (gitignored).
